subject: social_science

concepts.title: Kinship and Economic Patterns of Tribal Communities
concepts.definition: Communities organized around shared lineage and communal resource management, maintaining distinct traditions outside orthodox Varna social orders.
concepts.key_idea: Tribal groups sustained autonomy through joint landholding, ancestral ties, and resource combination.
question_patterns: how did tribal societies structure their land and resource allocation in Class 7 history
explain the role of kinship bonds in tribal livelihoods
what features distinguished tribal communities from caste-based societies
describe how tribal groups combined agriculture, hunting, and pastoralism
in what ways did tribal groups preserve their cultural independence

solution_steps.explain: Tribal communities were united by kinship ties and jointly controlled land and pasture resources.
Livelihoods combined agriculture, pastoral herding, and hunting-gathering based on local geography.

concepts.title: Regional Distribution of Subcontinent Tribes
concepts.definition: The geographic spread of prominent indigenous lineages such as Khokhars, Gakkhars, Nagas, Cheros, Bhils, and Gonds across varied ecological zones.
concepts.key_idea: Tribal groups dominated diverse habitats from mountainous frontiers to dense central forests.
question_patterns: where were the major tribal groups located across the Indian subcontinent in medieval times
identify the regions controlled by the Khokhars, Gakkhars, and Balochis
which tribes inhabited the north-eastern and eastern parts of India
describe the territorial presence of Cheros, Mundas, and Santals
explain the geographic spread of the Bhils and Kolis in western India

solution_steps.action: Map tribal lineages to geographic zones
solution_steps.explain: Khokhars and Gakkhars inhabited Punjab; Balochis in the north-west; Gaddis in western Himalayas; Nagas and Ahoms in the north-east.

solution_steps.action: Locate central and southern tribal groups
solution_steps.explain: Cheros, Mundas, and Santals held territories in Bihar, Jharkhand, and Orissa, while Bhils and Gonds spanned western and central India.

concepts.title: Nomadic Pastoralism and Itinerant Service Groups
concepts.section: How Nomads and Mobile People Lived
concepts.definition: Mobile populations moving across pastoral territories with animal herds while exchanging animal products with settled farmers for agricultural goods.
concepts.key_idea: Seasonal movement allowed pastoralists to trade animal produce for grain and crafted items.
question_patterns: how did nomadic pastoralists sustain their livelihood in medieval India
what goods were exchanged between mobile herders and settled agricultural communities
describe the activities of petty pedlars and itinerant groups in rural areas
explain the economic interaction between pastoral nomads and farmers
how did mobile communities transport their animals and goods across regions

solution_steps.explain: Pastoral nomads provided milk, wool, and ghee to settled farmers in exchange for grain, cloth, and utensils.

solution_steps.action: Identify itinerant trade and service groups
solution_steps.explain: Pedlars made and sold mats, ropes, and sacks, while entertainers and mendicants moved between villages for sustenance.

concepts.title: The Banjara Nomad Traders and Tanda System
concepts.section: How Nomads and Mobile People Lived
concepts.definition: A specialized merchant nomadic community organized into traveling caravans called tandas that carried grain across long distances for markets and military forces.
concepts.key_idea: Banjaras linked rural food production with urban supply chains and imperial campaigns.
question_patterns: who were the Banjaras and what was their role in trade
explain the concept and structure of a Banjara tanda
how did imperial rulers like Alauddin Khalji and Jahangir utilize Banjaras
describe Peter Mundy's historical observations regarding the Banjara lifestyle
what made the Banjaras vital for military logistics and town markets

solution_steps.explain: Banjaras traveled as merchant caravans called tandas, transporting grain using thousands of bullocks.
They bought grain in cheap markets, sold it in high-demand towns, and supplied armies during large military operations.

concepts.title: Emergence of Jatis and Caste Stratification
concepts.section: Changing Society: New Castes and Hierarchies
concepts.definition: Sub-caste formations arising from specialized occupational roles and the integration of tribal and artisan groups into the Varna structural framework.
concepts.key_idea: Economic specialization replaced broader varna classifications with detailed sub-caste hierarchies.
question_patterns: how did new jatis emerge within the traditional varna system
what was the significance of the Uyyakondan Udaiyar inscription regarding rathakaras
explain how specialized artisans were integrated into caste society
why did jati become the primary basis for social organization
describe how tribal groups were incorporated as lower status jatis

solution_steps.action: Trace the origin of specialized jatis
solution_steps.explain: As economic needs expanded, specialized crafts like smithing, carpentry, and masonry were recognized as distinct jatis by Brahmanas.
Inscriptions like that of Uyyakondan Udaiyar show assembly deliberations determining occupational statuses for groups like chariot-makers (rathakaras).

concepts.title: Rajput Lineages and Social Elevation of Tribal Chiefs
concepts.section: Changing Society: New Castes and Hierarchies
concepts.definition: The process through which emerging warrior lineages and leading tribal families gained Kshatriya status through Brahmana endorsement and state formation.
concepts.key_idea: Political power enabled influential tribal rulers to transition into recognized Rajput ruling dynasties.
question_patterns: how did new Rajput clans rise to power during the eleventh and twelfth centuries
explain how tribal ruling families attained Kshatriya status
why did dominant tribes in Punjab and Sind reject the orthodox caste system
what role did Brahmana support play in elevating tribal elites to ruling status
describe the relationship between state formation and Rajput social mobility

solution_steps.explain: Various ruling lineages including Hunas, Chandelas, and Chalukyas established powerful states and gained Rajput recognition.

solution_steps.action: Differentiate regional responses to caste hierarchy
solution_steps.explain: Leading tribal families joined the ruling elite with Brahmana support, while tribes in Punjab, Sind, and the North-West adopted Islam and rejected caste rules.

concepts.title: Gond Kingdom Village Administrative Structure
concepts.definition: A hierarchical administrative framework in Gondwana dividing a kingdom into garhs, where each garh contained chaurasis of 84 villages subdivided into barhots of 12 villages.
concepts.key_idea: Gond administrative hierarchy systematically grouped villages into units of 84 and 12.
question_patterns: in Class 7 history how many total villages are in a Gond kingdom division with num_chaurasi chaurasis
calculate the total number of villages in num_chaurasi chaurasis under the Gond administrative system
find the total village count for num_chaurasi chaurasi units in Garha Katanga
determine how many villages make up num_chaurasi chaurasis in Gondwana
what is the total number of villages across num_chaurasi chaurasi administrative divisions

solution_steps.action: Calculate total villages from chaurasi count
solution_steps.explain: Each chaurasi administrative unit contains exactly 84 villages.

concepts.title: Rise and Mughal Conquest of Garha Katanga
concepts.definition: The political trajectory of the prosperous central Indian Gond state that accumulated wealth through elephant trading before Mughal conquest under Asaf Khan.
concepts.key_idea: Garha Katanga achieved regional prominence under Rani Durgawati before facing Mughal invasion.
question_patterns: describe the political organization and wealth of Garha Katanga
what was the role of Rani Durgawati in defending the Gond kingdom
how did Garha Katanga generate its economic wealth
explain the Mughal campaign against Garha Katanga led by Asaf Khan
what happened to the Gond kingdom after its defeat by the Mughals

solution_steps.explain: Garha Katanga accumulated vast wealth by capturing and exporting wild elephants to neighboring kingdoms.
Rani Durgawati offered fierce resistance against Asaf Khan's Mughal forces in 1565; after her defeat, Mughals annexed key territories.

concepts.title: Ahom State Structure and Forced Labor System
concepts.definition: A centralized administrative organization in Assam where adult males called paiks performed mandatory state labor and served in military forces organized under clan units called khels.
concepts.key_idea: The Ahom state maintained infrastructure and defense through rotational compulsory public labor.
question_patterns: how was the paik system organized in the Ahom state
explain the function of clan units called khels in Ahom administration
describe how population census and relocation affected Ahom clan structures
what military and public works duties were assigned to adult male paiks
how did the Ahom state maintain centralized control through forced labor

solution_steps.action: Explain the paik forced labor requirement
solution_steps.explain: Villages were required to supply paiks by rotation based on population censuses, breaking up old clan concentrations.
Paiks served as soldiers during wartime and built dams, irrigation canals, and public works during peacetime.

concepts.title: Ahom Cultural Evolution and Buranji Historical Chronicles
concepts.definition: The cultural synthesis in medieval Assam characterized by royal patronage of literature, temple land grants, and official prose historical registers written in Ahom and Assamese.
concepts.key_idea: Ahom statecraft fostered sophisticated literary records called Buranjis alongside regional Hindu adoption.
question_patterns: what were Buranjis and why were they important in Ahom history
how did Hinduism influence the Ahom monarchy during Sib Singh's rule
describe the literary and cultural achievements of Ahom society
in what languages were the historical Buranjis written
explain how Ahom rulers balanced traditional beliefs with Brahmana influence

solution_steps.explain: Under Sib Singh, Hinduism became prominent and Brahmanas received royal land grants, though traditional ancestral beliefs persisted.
Buranjis were official historical works composed first in the Ahom language and subsequently translated into Assamese.

solution_template.explain: There are 84 villages in one chaurasi unit
